A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, bias analyses, intervention and scaling experiments, and human verification, including results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original contamination and evaluation-reliability analyses in Sections 6.2–6.3.

M1.justification: The Unbiased Evaluator, BOAT interventions, combination constraints and probing procedure are unchanged. Cross-generation and cross-checking in v2 Section 7 are explicitly future directions, not implemented components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ARC-C, MMLU and GSM8K with the same task coverage. The new fine-tuning study retains MMLU; LiveBench supplies published aggregate reference scores rather than additional task evaluations. Open-ended extensions remain future work.

E2.justification: v2 newly uses published LiveBench results as an empirical comparison reference for model rankings in Section 6.3 and Table 4; v1 only cited LiveBench. Existing vanilla and minimal Agents-as-an-Evaluator comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds a controlled protocol comparing Llama2-13B before and after fine-tuning on MMLU test samples, under vanilla and Unbiased evaluation. It also adds correlations between averaged benchmark scores and LiveBench scores for five overlapping models. Existing five-shot, temperature-zero and 1000-token settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 6.2–6.3 add deliberate test-set contamination and external ranking-reliability analyses. These substantially extend validation by directly testing contamination sensitivity and agreement with an external evaluation reference. Earlier bias, intervention, scaling, confusion-matrix and human-verification analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Five-run averaging, the main table's uncertainty reporting and Table 1's correlation p-values are unchanged. New Tables 3–4 provide point estimates without introducing additional uncertainty estimates, run counts or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports vanilla/Unbiased scores of 55.6/33.7 before test-set fine-tuning and 96.6/37.1 afterward. New Table 4 reports LiveBench Pearson/Kendall correlations of 0.918/0.600 for vanilla and 0.949/1.000 for Unbiased evaluation. These add substantive findings about contamination sensitivity and ranking reliability; existing benchmark, bias and human-verification results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The bias definitions, Proposition 3.1, causal formulation and Equations 1–13 are unchanged. The same proof moves from Appendix C in v1 to Appendix D in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a bias decomposition, identification of data and model biases, and the Unbiased Evaluator. The additional validation does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly attributes accuracy reductions to reduced contamination and interprets LiveBench agreement as supporting alignment with human judgments. It also adds prospective applicability to open-ended tasks through rule-based interventions, cross-generation and cross-checking. These interpretations and extensions were absent from v1.

D1.justification: For the new reliability analysis, v2 identifies the LiveBench snapshot dated 2024-11-25, its global-average scores and the exclusion of GPT-4-Turbo and Yi1.5-34B-Chat. Existing implementation settings, prompts and BOAT constraints are retained. Fine-tuning hyperparameters are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yang et al. (2023) to motivate the contamination experiment and positions its approach against LiveBench's recurring update costs. The added 2025 LiveBench reference describes the same work already cited in its 2024 form; the related-work sections otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an explicit Agents-as-an-Evaluator definition, groups supplementary experiments under a dedicated Ablations section, introduces Future Work and reorganizes the appendices. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1, adds Tables 3–4, moves the BOAT demonstration into Appendix A and moves human-verification results into the main text. It also expands captions and abbreviates appendix table labels. Existing result plots and the overall document format are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence about resistance to deliberate test-set contamination and agreement with external rankings, strengthening support missing from v1. The gains are limited by absent fine-tuning details and a five-model LiveBench comparison. These additions do not establish v2's broader attribution of all accuracy drops to contamination or its claimed alignment with human judgments.
